newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire shares plunge after Granada bid denial.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire shares plunge after Granada bid denial.

text.p: Shares in British commercial television (ITV) company Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc fell more than 10 percent on Thursday after neighbour Granada Group Plc ruled out a bid for the moment.
"Reports of the possibility of Granada making an offer for Yorkshire at or above the current market share price are misplaced," media and leisure company Granada said.

"Granada confirms that, unless there is a material change in Yorkshire's circumstances (including an offer from a third party), it has no current intention of making an offer for Yorkshire," the company added in a statement.
Granada has taken advantage of a relaxation of UK media ownership to build up a total stake of around 27 percent in Yorkshire and a full bid has long been anticipated.
Yorkshire chairman Ward Thomas said this week that a takeover bid for his company should be pitched as high as 17 pounds ($27.30) per share.
The Granada statement sent Yorkshire shares plunging earthwards, touching a low of 10.75 pounds at one point before closing at 11.40 pounds, 1.40 off on the day.

Bid speculation has helped to fuel a rise of more than 80 percent in Yorkshire's share price over the last 14 months and the company was valued at in excess of 800 million pounds before the Granada statement.
Yorkshire chairman Thomas said this week that he believed a bid from Granada was "extremely likely".
United News & Media Plc , which operates ITV franchises for southern and eastern England, has a stake of some 14 percent in Yorkshire and is another potential predator.
The UK authorities last year lifted a two-licence ownership limit on ITV companies, clearing the way for the big three of Granada, United News and Carlton Communications Plc to tighten their grip.

Granada already operates the ITV franchises for north-west England and London Weekend Television. Yorkshire, which broadcasts to the northern cities of Leeds and Newcastle, this week announced a 40 percent rise in annual pre-tax profit to 30.2 million pounds. ($1=.6228 Pound)
